settings.heading: Settings
settings.paneNote: Agents, folder and permissions belong to each session — change them in its own bar. A new session starts where the last one was.
settings.newSessionsNote: Applies to sessions started from now on. The two agents do not share a model, so each has its own. A conversation already open keeps what it started with.
settings.completionDeepseekNote: Grey text in the editor, offered as you type and inserted only when you press Tab. This is a separate credential from the one the DeepSeek agent uses, so the two can be rotated apart. Choosing DeepSeek here sends the code around your cursor to DeepSeek on every pause in typing — the same file contents an agent would read, so do not set a key in a project you would not let an agent open. It is encrypted with your login keychain and never leaves this machine except to DeepSeek. Chorus cannot show it back to you: remove it and enter a new one to change it.
settings.completionCodestralNote: Grey text in the editor, offered as you type and inserted only when you press Tab. Mistral's own completion service, separate from every other credential here. Choosing Codestral sends the code around your cursor to Mistral on every pause in typing, and nothing is sent at all if you pick it without a key — there is no quiet fallback to another provider. It is encrypted with your login keychain. Chorus cannot show it back to you: remove it and enter a new one to change it.
settings.explainNote: Every finished reply gets an Explain simply button, which asks the agent to say the whole answer again plainly in this language. Select part of a reply and it can also translate that passage into it. Write the language however you like — “Arabic”, “Lebanese Arabic”, “simple Arabic”. An explanation follows what you write; a translation uses the standard written form of the language. Technical terms stay in English either way — event, status, props, a file name — so what you read still matches the code. Leave it empty and neither is offered. This does not change Chorus's own language.
settings.deepseekNote: DeepSeek runs through the claude CLI you already have, pointed at DeepSeek's own endpoint — there is nothing extra to install. The key is encrypted with your login keychain and never leaves this machine except to DeepSeek. Chorus cannot show it back to you: remove it and enter a new one to change it. Your Claude account is not touched and its limits are not used.
settings.typesafeInstalled: The skill is installed. Claude and DeepSeek can use it — they share the same configuration.
settings.typesafeNoCli: The claude CLI was not found, so there is nothing to install into.
settings.typesafeUnconfirmed: The commands ran without error, but the skill could not be confirmed. Open Settings again to check.
settings.typesafeVerifyCost: Testing the key sends one real request, which uses tokens on your TypeSafe account. TypeSafe has no free endpoint to check against, so Chorus never does this on its own.
settings.typesafeVerifyMissing: There is no key stored to test.
settings.typesafeRejected: TypeSafe refused the key. Remove it and enter a new one.
settings.typesafeMalformed: TypeSafe rejected the request Chorus sent. Your key is not the problem — this is a bug in Chorus.
settings.typesafeBusy: TypeSafe is rate-limiting this account right now. The key was not tested. Try again shortly.
settings.typesafeUnreachable: TypeSafe could not be reached, so the key was not tested.
settings.typesafeNote: TypeSafe is not an agent — it is a service your agents can call to classify text, score it against a rubric, or answer a yes-or-no question. Saving the key here puts it in the environment of every agent Chorus starts, so they can use it without you pasting it into a conversation. The key is encrypted with your login keychain and never leaves this machine except to TypeSafe. Chorus cannot show it back to you: remove it and enter a new one to change it.
settings.notifications: Notify when an agent needs a decision
settings.styleNote: Bilingual replies come as paired paragraphs: one in English, then the same paragraph in Modern Standard Arabic, with technical terms, file names and identifiers left in English on both sides. It is off unless you ask for it. Each conversation also has its own switch in the composer — Plain or Bilingual — so you can read in Arabic in one room and leave another plain because you are pasting its replies to someone else. Flipping that switch restarts the room's agents on the same thread: nothing is lost and nothing is re-read, but the change lands on the next reply rather than one already arriving.

traffic.empty: Start capture above, then point the app's API base URL at this machine.

traffic.originHint: The real backend. Your app's calls go here.
traffic.portHint: Chorus listens here. Your app points at this.
traffic.envVarHint: Copy the line below into this variable.
traffic.originFailed: That address was refused. It has to be an absolute http or https URL.
traffic.portInUse: Port {{port}} is already in use — another Chorus, or something else, is holding it.
traffic.accessLoopbackHint: Only this machine can reach the listener.
traffic.accessLanHint: The default. Anything on this network can reach your backend through Chorus, which does not check who is asking. The first Start asks the system to allow incoming connections.
traffic.noTerminal: Choose a terminal above to read its output.
traffic.waiting: Nothing yet. Only what a terminal writes from now on is captured, so one already running stays quiet until its next line.
traffic.legacyQuestion: A shared connection was saved before projects had endpoints of their own. Keep it as it is, or start fresh?
traffic.lagging: This view fell behind the capture and stopped receiving updates.
traffic.sourceBusy: Another project is capturing the device log. Release it there first.
traffic.unknownProject: That project is no longer in the registry.
traffic.noPort: This project has no port of its own yet.
traffic.noOrigin: Set the address to forward to before starting capture.
traffic.ownershipUnknown: A saved connection is on a port that could not be read, so no project can be given one yet.
traffic.unresolved: The saved connection could not be read, so it cannot be assigned yet.
traffic.noSelection: Pick a call above to see its request and response.

bodyNote.evicted: These bodies were dropped to make room for newer ones.
